approach: backfill the whole clibuilder surface as its own mission, chosen by the Council over a scoped root-plus-touched-nodes cut
capability-first layout, ten nodes, colocated per the args-minus precedent
partition-quality measured and declined to decide; layout follows the recommendation, not the numbers
the zod removal that prompted this is deferred to a later mission

summary: replace zod with Standard Schema for configuration plus an in-house type descriptor for arguments and options, and stop re-exporting z from the public entry point
why: the framework pins every consumer to its own validator major, and the validator is its heaviest runtime dependency on a package that optimizes startup

summary: an option's `default` is not type-checked against its declared `type`
why: cli.Command.Options is Record<Name, Options.Entry<Type>> with Type defaulting to z.ZodType<any> and never inferred per entry, so Entry's `default?: z.infer<Type>` widens to any. `{ type: z.array(z.string()), default: 5 }` compiles and the option still types as string[], so run receives a value its own declaration says is impossible. Closing it needs per-entry inference of Type; verified against ts/cli.ts during the command-definition backfill.
